query: For CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain whether a stable, coherent protective oxide layer forms and persists during exposure above 900 °C in an oxidative or corrosive atmosphere, rather than developing unstable surface oxides that crack or spall? Specify what governs the behaviour and why, a controlled comparison against a defined baseline, the predicted differences, the applicable exposure and material-state boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a falsifying observation.

generation.hypothesis: The formation and stability of a protective oxide layer on CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) is governed by the grain size and distribution of elements, which can be controlled through processing techniques such as annealing and homogenization.
generation.material_initial_state: CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) in a single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state
generation.intervention: Grain size control through processing techniques (e.g., annealing, homogenization) and exposure to oxidative atmosphere at 900 °C
generation.conditions: Temperature: 900 °C, Atmosphere: Oxidative, Exposure time: Up to 100 hours, Processing parameters: Optimized for each alloy composition
generation.structural_mediator: Grain size and distribution of elements
generation.mechanism: The grain size and distribution of elements influence the formation and stability of the protective oxide layer. A finer grain size and more uniform distribution of elements can lead to a more stable and coherent oxide layer, while a coarser grain size and non-uniform distribution can lead to a less stable oxide layer.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloys with a finer grain size and more uniform distribution of elements will exhibit improved high-temperature corrosion resistance compared to alloys with a coarser grain size and non-uniform distribution. The baseline alloy will exhibit intermediate behavior.
generation.baseline: CrFeCoNiX high-entropy alloys (X = Si, Mn, or Al) without grain size control
generation.boundary: The applicable exposure and material-state boundaries are temperature (900 °C), atmosphere (oxidative), and exposure time (up to 100 hours). The material-state boundary is the single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution state.
